sources.entry: Kivy - An open-source cross-platform GUI framework for desktop, mobile, and embedded devices.

summary.one_liner: Kivy is an open-source, MIT-licensed Python framework for building multitouch GUI apps that run across desktop, mobile, and embedded platforms from one codebase.
summary.what_it_does: Kivy is a Python framework, written in Python and Cython, for developing GUI applications. It is built on OpenGL ES 2.0 and supports various input devices. It includes an extensible widget library in which all widgets support multitouch. The README says one codebase can target Windows, macOS, Linux (including Raspberry Pi OS), Android, and iOS. The README also points to a set of sibling projects: Buildozer for packaging apps, Plyer for hardware access, PyJNIus and Pyobjus for calling Java and Objective-C, Python for Android, Kivy iOS for building iOS toolchains, and others. Installation docs, tutorials, an API reference, and examples are referenced in the README, with examples in the examples folder.
use_cases: build cross-platform desktop GUI apps in Python
create touchscreen or multitouch user interfaces
package Python apps for Android or iOS
GUI for Raspberry Pi or embedded devices
accessing hardware features via Plyer from a Kivy app
notable: One codebase targets Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS
All widgets are built with multitouch support
Extensive ecosystem of sibling projects for packaging and hardware access
Ships with many examples in the examples folder
Includes Roboto fonts and a virtual keyboard
caveats: README does not include install commands; installation details are in external docs
Mobile and embedded targets rely on additional sibling tools such as Buildozer or Kivy iOS
keywords: make a phone app in python
